text:
alan_support: customer tenant `acme-marketing` saw monthly credits drop to 0 at 03:12 PST, ~2 hours before their expected local midnight refill. They hit repeated 429s and claimed a promo top-up earlier today. Logs show refill job ran, DB shows credits added, but API still returns 429 for several minutes.

maya_product: thanks for flagging. do we know if this is single-tenant or org-wide? any recent tenant migrations? :thinking_face:

alan_support: single tenant. they upgraded a promo this morning, +5M tokens. billing records show +5M at 02:05 PST. refill job for monthly buckets ran at 00:00 UTC as usual.

jen_sre: can you paste the API error and a short repro? also any relevant headers (x-credits, x-cache-hit)?

alan_support: here's the error body the user saw repeatedly: `{"error":"quota_exhausted","code":429,"message":"monthly credits exhausted"}` Headers from proxied requests: `x-credits-remaining: 0`, `x-cache-status: MISS` initially, then `x-cache-status: HIT` after ~4m, still 429 until 6m.

liam_infra: suspicious — DB shows +5M immediately but the in-memory per-tenant counters live in redis and we have a local in-process cache in the API service with a 5m TTL. if refill writes to DB and redis but service instance still has cached 0, you get visible 0 until TTL expires or service invalidates cache.

alan_support: customer reported they restarted their long-running streaming session and still hit 429s.

jen_sre: restart wouldn't clear in-process cache. can we verify whether refill writes publish a cache-invalidate event on the pubsub channel? last infra change replaced the pubsub lib in dedicated hosts.

liam_infra: checking. refill job is billing/refill-monthly v3. It writes DB, then publishes `billing.refills` with tenant id. consumers are api-service (invalidate redis/inproc) and metrics-collector. Looking at logs, billing job emitted event at 02:05:12 PST, redis accepted the new counter, but api-service on the customer's host logged pubsub subscription error for a short window: `err=EOF` at 02:05:10->02:05:45 (connection flapped during a rolling deploy). That matches ~4m of visible miss then eventual HIT.

maya_product: so sequence is: billing job adds credits -> event published -> some API instances didn't receive the event due to transient pubsub flapping -> those instances kept returning cached 0 until TTL. Is that right?

liam_infra: yes. additional wrinkle: promo top-ups go through a different code-path that updates a per-route burst allowance key (burst_tokens:<tenant>) in redis and also increments the monthly bucket. due to a race the refill event was published before the burst key write completed for this tenant. the api-service checks both keys; if burst key missing and local monthly cache = 0 -> 429. once burst key is present and/or cache invalidated, requests succeed.

alan_support: customer impact: 6-8 minutes of 429s after a successful top-up. They expect near-instant availability after top-up.

jen_sre: mitigation: 1) lower in-process cache TTL to 30s for credit counters (hotfix), 2) make billing job write-order atomic: burst key first, then publish event, 3) make API side fall back to redis read on cache MISS rather than trust inproc value if header `x-force-refresh=true` present.

liam_infra: I can push cache TTL change in a canary now. also will add a short retry-on-429 guidance for support.

alan_support: repro steps for ENG if helpful:
```
# simulate tenant with long streaming session holding cached 0
# 1) set inproc cache to 0
# 2) write DB + redis refill
# 3) simulate pubsub disconnect for api instance
# 4) send request -> expect 429 until inproc TTL expires
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

maya_product: nice repro. please include logs and the `billing.refills` event id when you open the postmortem. i'll draft a short customer note: apologize, explain root cause (cache + pubsub race), outline fixes + ETA.

auto-billing-bot: billing.refills event 12345 processed, tenant=acme-marketing, delta=+5000000, processed_by=billing-03

alan_support: next steps: liam will roll canary with reduced cache TTL and add defensive redis fallback; jen will add a postmortem; maya will own customer comms. I'll update thread with timeline.

liam_infra: canary rolling now to 10% hosts. monitoring alert on `credit-visible-lag` set to fire if >30s for >1m.

jen_sre: grabbing logs and preparing postmortem template. thanks all.

alan_support: customer notified of workaround: reconnect streaming session or hit a small read-only endpoint to force cache refresh. they accepted and we unblocked them. :white_check_mark:
